sources.entry: BibaVPN | Self-hosted SOCKS5 and HTTP CONNECT tunnel over TLS and WebSocket for single-VPS deployments

summary.one_liner: BibaVPN is an experimental self-hosted Rust tunnel that carries SOCKS5 and HTTP CONNECT traffic over TLS and WebSocket to a server you run on your own VPS.
summary.what_it_does: The project provides a Rust server and CLI client that forward local SOCKS5 and optional HTTP CONNECT proxy traffic through an encrypted TLS plus WebSocket tunnel to a VPS you control. SOCKS5 UDP relay is supported over a separate WebSocket session. The default tunnel adds ChaCha20-Poly1305 encryption, authenticated control frames and padding inside TLS. Configuration covers traffic shaping (padding, jitter, decoy traffic, TLS profiles), 1–4 parallel TCP WebSocket sessions, certificate pinning, and an optional camouflage website on the same TLS port. Encrypted biba:// invitation URIs let other devices connect using a passphrase. Desktop and Android apps are included, and an optional REALITY handshake mode is described as BibaVPN's own protocol rather than Xray-compatible.
use_cases: self-hosted VPN on a single VPS
route browser traffic through a personal proxy
SOCKS5 proxy with DNS through the tunnel
share connection settings with another device via invitation
tunnel HTTP CONNECT traffic for proxy-aware tools
test a tunnel locally with Docker
how_to_run: git clone the repository and cd into BibaVPN
export BIBA_VPN_TOKEN and BIBA_VPN_PSK with openssl rand, then run: docker compose -f docker-compose.hub.yml up -d (local lab)
notable: SOCKS5 and HTTP CONNECT tunnel over TLS + WebSocket with padding and timing jitter
Encrypted biba:// invitation URIs protected by a passphrase (Argon2id in v2 format)
Camouflage website served on the same TLS port
Multiplexed TCP streams across 1–4 WebSocket sessions
Prebuilt-image Docker lab for trying the full tunnel locally
caveats: Experimental and evolving; protocol not frozen and has no third-party security audit
DPI resistance depends on network and configuration and is not a guarantee
iOS app is unfinished: the Packet Tunnel extension does not forward traffic yet; the CLI only proxies apps configured to use it rather than capturing all traffic
